text:
We have moved to this App from Konnect. I am noticing a lot of interference, dropped out calls and instability. 

This is very frustrating and causes huge anxiety to my father who panics every time he can’t reach me. 

There are clearly some bugs and it’s not clear sound. Other people appear on screen in call and loud ringing noises in background 

There is no ringing sound when I ring people in my care window so I never know until they pick up. I would like to see photo sharing also as this is a very necessary feature. 

The concept is great but the product currently has instability and unreliability issues from my experience. Hopefully these issues can be addressed.

title: Roy’s lifeline
text: We purchased the Komp subscription in 2020. Occasional teething problems and loss of connection from time to time but this has been a lifeline between my family and my father in his care home throughout lockdown. We still chat every day and he has been able to watch his great grandson develop from a newborn in 2020 to now. Little Henry has got to know dad this way where he might otherwise have been a stranger. Dad is now unable to walk so the family can come to him and send him photos of their lives. I don’t know what we would do without it. I can monitor dads moods and physical health and chat to his carers as they pop in with his tea etc. these things would be impossible on a normal phone call. I do wish I could post videos of Henry’s development but we watch them on my phone when I visit. There is a slight drawback in that he is immobile so the Komp must remain in exactly the right place to see him in his armchair. If the cleaner moves it by mistake I can’t see him fully. But we have guide tape on the floor and table to show where things need to be.  I’m amazed there are no other residents or indeed anyone I’ve met who has even heard of the Komp. I feel like an unofficial ambassador for the company as I tell people how wonderful it is whenever I meet someone who might benefit. Thank you so much. Diane Gittings.  From Kent and Sussex in the UK.

title: Window to the world
text:
Before we discovered the KOMP device, I had long wished that just such a thing would come along and thanks to No Isolation, my wish eventually became reality.
If you are an elderly, or disabled person for whom using a PC, laptop or notebook for communications is difficult and for whom a mere telephone cannot provide the pleasure of face-to-face contact with friends and family, then KOMP is the answer.
Supremely simple and fuss free to use (no technical knowledge or experience required), the KOMP allows you to enjoy chats with loved ones at any time you wish as well as the possibility of seeing their photographs and receiving text messages on screen.
All of this is done on a high quality stand alone screen (very similar to a smallish TV).
When friends call, as long as you have the unit switched on you will hear a countdown tone for 10 beats along wit the name of whoever of your invited friends (no strangers can call you) then you will see them and be able to talk to them as a video call.
It’s simple, reliable, trouble free and great fun and it’s the perfect answer for maintaining contact without the hassle of computers, mobiles and other such devices.
I had one for my bedbound mum-in-law and I also have one for my own mum. Both families are great fans of the KOMP and during the current crisis it became even more essential than normal. Will would never want to be without this device and I cannot recommend it highly enough!

title: Life changing & huge screen
text:
We sadly lost our Mum recently & Dad became too poorly to care at home so he now lives in a residential home, caring & lovely people but obviously missing life with us. It’s been a tough time. We all visit on a regular basis & on good days take him out…..He struggles with his phone so I wanted something easy & found Komp, all I can say is it’s made such a huge difference for several reasons. 1/ we can send messages & texts & viewing on a large screen makes a big difference 2/ We can video call so he can see us clearly, the sound is excellent too 3/ He called us from his phone one evening saying he was poorly so we got on the Komp to see & reassure him a nurse was on her way to him 4/ We send funny jokes too which brightens his day. We like that it just has 1 button, on, off & sound. I think all care homes could look at installing these into their living rooms for everyone to gain access 
🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟 So impressed & I must be as I never leave reviews. Thank you
Debs

バイタルを気にする自分にとっての大事な相棒です！！コレからもよろしくお願いします！

提案としてはストレスチェックも入れてもらうと、脳疾患の自分の役に立つので、次のアップデートで採用してくれたら嬉しいので期待しております！
睡眠傾向とかも掴んでくれるそんな相棒ならもっと頼れるので、オールしがちな場合は大抵夜型とか、時差ボケ状態であればどこの人間と同じ生活をしているのか分かって面白いと思ったので、よろしくお願いします！！

title: 便利だけど…
text:
子供の病状などを手軽に記載できるのは便利。
だけど、不満な点も何点か。
1.記載内容がアウトプット出来ない。
アプリから日付でピンポイントでチェックしないと、記載内容が見られない。
人毎にまとめてテキスト出力できると時系列で病状が把握できるし、せっかく書いたデータの汎用性も高くなる。

2.ステータス？のバリエーションが少ない
メモの内容がわかりやすいように用意されてると思われる絵柄の種類が少ない。
どうせ用意するなら、もう少しバリエーションがないと使いづらい。
絵柄が用意できないなら、ユーザーが任意でステータスを指定できる項目があれば、より使い勝手が良くなりと思う。

欲を言えば、体温が折れ線グラフになると体温の上がり下がりが診察時に伝えやすくていいなと思います。また、日毎に一覧にした際、横にスクロールで日付を横断できたら見やすいです。
でも、無料でこれなら満足です！こらからもお世話になります。

医師に不快な顔をされたので
昨晩熱を出した際にはメモ帳で記録
その後アプリを探して此方に来ました。
他の方が書かれてるようにアイコンが増えたり(食事や睡眠)

text:
ミーテが使えなくなるので、代わりになるようなアプリを探してこちらを入手。
広告が画面に出るのですが、ある広告は、エリアを白黒画面を反転させる広告で、非常に不快。イヤでも目には入りますが、目障り過ぎてアプリを使う気なくしました。
因みに、ミーテは継続使用が出来るようになったので、PCとのデータ連携やデータダウンロードを求めなければ、携帯上で継続使用出来ますよ。

title: アイコンが少なすぎ

ただアイコンの数が少なすぎていまいち後から見たときにわかりにくいと思います。
もう少しアイコンの数が痩せることができたらよかったと思いました。

title: シンプルで使いやすい
text:
体調が優れないので専用に
記録できるアプリを探していました。
主に体温や服用した薬、症状をメモすることが目的なのでサッと記録できて満足しています。
欲を言えば検索を含めてのタグ機能、
新規作成時のアイコンの種類を増やして頂けると嬉しいです。

title: 探してました！
text:
体温の入力とメモが簡単に出来て、助かります！
父の闘病中の日常管理として、使わせて頂きます。
メモに写真も付けれると更に嬉しいです！！！
期待を込めて★4つです。

title: ありがとうございます！！

子ども達が良く夜中に熱を出すので、メモを取るのに大変で、、、座薬等の時間の把握も困ってました(>_<)

携帯さえあれば簡単に入力できるなんてほんと嬉しいです！！

The button has fallen out of my Fossil Hybrid HR (FTW7026), on December 6 , 2024. This is the second time this has happened to me, I returned the first watch to Amazon the first time, and it was quickly replaced (December 26, 2023).

Because this is the 2nd time this has happened, I believe there exists an inherent weakness in this design, and that suspicion is reinforced by the fact that Fossil seems to have discontinued the product.

title: Music Controls keep changing for the worse
text: Please give us the ability to assign our own music controls in the music control mode, or at the last, the option to revert to different formats. I've loved my Fossil Hybrid HR for the ~2y I've had it, but the several changes to music controls in recent months have continued to make it worse and worse for me. ... The middle button - which previously served both to pause (tap) and the return to home (hold) - was simplified to only performing the latter in all modes.  Not only does this lower the number of available quickly-accesses modes from 3 to 2, it also forces a remap of the 5 music control functions onto the remaining 4 input options, complicating the inputs mostly at the expense of the least used one (for the avg. customers): the rewind. ... While I'm surely an outlier, this was the watch's main function for me since I use it primarily for audiobook rewinds. Rewinds have gone from requiring taps (<1 sec); to requiring to holds (~1 sec); to requiring a hold to pause, holds to rewind, and a final hold to play again (>5 sec). Audiobook readers may require 1-10 presses per minute if a particular passage or line is difficult to understand. The feedback is also not instantaneous, so unlike before where I'll immediately hear the next words upon tapping/holding, I have to unpause to check where in the passage I am. What used to take <5 sec to input may take >20 now. This delay, along with the finicking with controls back and forth, disrupt my comprehension of I'm trying to understand, and so I probably end up taking 10x longer to get through difficult passages now. Simply put, it's not worth the effort and I just get my phone out now, so I don't use the smartwatch for anything but checking the time now. Fossil is great outside of this, but it does hurt to be in a niche group of customer that may be ignored.

When I first got this watch years ago, this was great. Then I started noticing last year that the sync was no longer working. I’d load up the app and it would instantly crash or just wouldn’t connect with my phone. They finally updated to its current version and I was able to sync, but now my data is lost from the day before if I don’t sync before midnight. Pretty stupid since I was out walking from evening until 4am, and I lost tens of thousands of steps. That’s fine if your routine allows, but if I’m on a night shift, I won’t have time to interrupt work just to sit and wait for my watch to sync. If I’m on vacation, I’m not going to whip out my phone at the club just to catch the last few moments that I can keep my steps. 

I love my hybrid watch since it was a gift from a loved one, but this has been a terrible experience in the past few years. As mentioned if you’re cool with the idea of your data getting wiped from your watch before you can sync, then fine. The app can keep one star. But I’m over it and plan to move on.

title: The 5.0 update ruined this app
text:
I recently purchased a fossil HR hybrid, and was very happy with it for about 2 weeks, until they updated to the new version of the app. The Home Screen on the app is now full of ads to buy watch bands and more watches, which is absurd considering that I already have the watch, and owning 2 of the same would make no sense at all. Previously , it showed your health data, which was a whole lot more useful, and is now hidden at the bottom of the screen, and needs to be tapped on to view. I understand why you want to promote your products in your app, but that’s not why I open it. Put those at the bottom, where they aren’t in the way of the actual functionality of your product. 

Additionally, they removed the ability to read more than 2 lines of a notification on the watch, removed the ability to see how far an where you walked/ran on the watch, ruined the music controls on the watch by putting them In multiple screens, removed many customization options for your watch faces, added useless menus that you need to navigate to view your health data on the watch (where before it could be configured to one button press), and removed the ability to see seconds on timers and stop watch, which makes the stopwatch feature completely useless. 

And despite a lot of feedback from long time users of their product, nobody seems to be able to get more than a canned response about their concerns from customer support. 

Fossil, if you actually read this review, please listen to your customers. You had an amazing product, but then you’ve neutered every useful feature with this update. Please consider adding these features (and others that I personally don’t use but were also removed ) back into your product.

title: App does not keep weather refreshed
text:
I do like the app for its appearance and usability, but the annoyance of the weather’s refresh overshadows the positive aspects. 

Every time I look at my watch (a Collider HR), the weather and chance of rain show two dashes, not synced. I have to go to my phone and open the app to get it to sync up. The app is configured to use precise location always, and it’s not closed, it’s running in the background. If I have to go to my phone to access the app and essentially force a sync with the watch, I might as well just open the weather app on my phone. 

The point of this watch is to lower the dependency of always getting your phone out. However it falls short.

title: It’s nice that Apple has decided to set a default timer for you
text:
All in all, I like the Apple Watch but a few updates ago Apple decided to set a default timer of 15 minutes on the watch. This is new behavior as prior to this, when you went to the timer you simply selected the timer you wanted and you were good to go. 

Now however, Apple has decided that whenever you launch the timer they will set a default timer of 15 minutes for you. How do they know I want a 15 minute timer? Their support site says they chose 15 minutes as it is a good compromise between various activities like working out or other things. I’ve never used my timer during workouts. I use it when I’m grilling, or other things none of which ever requires a 15 minute timer. So now, every time I use the timer, I have to cancel the default 15 minute timer and set it to what I actually want. 

Here’s an idea for you Apple, don’t assume anything for your customers, let us decide what timer we want. Either get rid of the default timer (which never used to be a thing) or if you insist on being our big brother and make decisions for us, then let us set our own default timer setting in settings. I frankly don’t want a default timer set every time I assume the app, I simply want to quickly and easily set my own timer. Assuming you know what is best for everyone and make decisions for your customers is completely arrogant. Worthless.

These watches are too expensive to lose functionality so early in their lifetime, and I have no desire to upgrade my watch every 3-4 years when it works perfectly fine. title: Fall detection? I call BS.
text:
I have my watch for multiple reasons. One of those being fall detection because I am a professional equestrian rider. I have fallen no less than a dozen times since purchasing my first watch with “fall detection.”

Most recently I have an Apple Watch Series 9. I have come off of a horse 3 times (HARD) while having this watch and none of those  times was there an emergency alert. However, I have clapped my hands excitedly for someone and also had a mild roll off of my body ball while stretching where my watch has gone off. What gives on when this thing registers? Do I have to pound my fist on the ground (if I’m conscious) after I’ve come off to get a fall to register? WTH Apple?

I realize that an accelerometer is the primary source that registers to tell the watch to make an emergency call, but Apple really should rethink their “fall detection.” 

My mother had several falls as an elderly obese person that were not registered. This was the absolute primary reason for the purchase. We had backup emergency buttons as well. 

I’ve had numerous hard hits to the ground from horses or otherwise and there has been no “fall” detected. 

I am well aware that this is not the end all be all in fall detection, but it fails nine times out of 10 in actual fall scenarios versus false positives for ridiculous everyday movements. 

Come on Apple, I know you can do better. I am absolutely happy to be a test subject for your fall detection upgrades since I continue to have many  instances in which it SHOULD register. 

My only saving grace is that, THANKFULLY,  the times I have come off, my cellular has worked. That is also a very sketchy issue. Cellular on the Apple Watch works at its own convenience.

title: Eight Isn’t Enough
text: We set up Caring Village for my family of 8 siblings to help monitor and manage our parent’s health. This site has everything we need and is so simple to use on your laptop, iPad or phone. The journal feature allows each of us to capture with our visits or calls with our parents to share with the family current health issues or follow up from doctor’s appointments. It’s so much better than just texting each other. We also use the Calendar feature to track appointments so that one of us can join them in person or on a call to make sure we capture all the notes for reference. The ability to upload documents and maintain all the information on each of their various Drs makes it really easy for us to coordinate. Most importantly, the team at Caring Village, particularly Linda, has been amazingly responsive whenever we needed clarify a process or make suggestions for improvements. Caring Village has been absolutely perfect for our family to be actively engaged in our parents health.

title: Caring Village is awesome

title: This app carried me through one of the hardest seasons of my life
text:
I spent the last few years caring for my mom while she was living with stage 4 lung cancer. Nothing truly prepares you for how overwhelming caregiving becomes — emotionally, physically, and mentally. Every day felt like a juggling act: driving back and forth for chemotherapy, managing medications, updating advance medical directives, coordinating travel so she could see friends and family, scheduling physical therapy, managing oxygen equipment, dealing with insurance and deductibles, and trying to secure medical appointments months in advance.

It was exhausting. And often, it felt very lonely.

Caring Village brought calm and clarity into a situation that otherwise felt like constant chaos. The medication management section alone was a godsend — one less thing to keep in my head when I was already running on fumes. Having a shared calendar to coordinate tasks gave structure to days that felt overwhelming, and being able to communicate with the caregiver we hired in the later months — all in one place — made an enormous difference.

What mattered most was the peace of mind. Caring Village helped me feel supported, organized, and less alone at a time when everything felt heavy. It dramatically lowered my stress and allowed me to be more present with my mom, instead of constantly worrying about what I might be forgetting.

This app is clearly built by people who understand caregiving not as a checklist, but as a deeply human experience. I’m profoundly grateful it existed when I needed it most.

Thank you, Caring Village.

title: Caring Village works
text: I used this app a couple years ago, and it was excellent.  As things progressed with my dad, unfortunately, the time passed where we used it actively. The app is great -- easy to use, and it clearly was built to do the things we need the most.  The name is right on -- it does take a Village to care for a family member, particularly as they become ill as a senior.  The various doctors, hospitals, EMRs (electronic med records), patient portals, pharmacies, etc. all seem to have their own way of doing things, and if there's one MAJOR lesson I've learned ... it's up to the family to play quarterback. Caring Village has been a tool that allows us to do that a lot easier, and for me and my 2 brothers to stay connected (the 3 of us are the key members of the village honestly, but docs and other folks are extended village members to us).  5 stars, and thank you Caring Village!

title: Bonnie S.
text:
I am a geriatric care manager and I discovered this app when I was trying to juggle communication among 30+ family members for one of my clients. I since have started several more “villages” for other clients and use most of the available options. Overall I love this app. I have the following observations to share in hopes it helps people make a decision about using this and also in hopes the developers are reading reviews

Pros: 
-ability to care plan and have staff document daily in the wellness journal to monitor compliance and communicate with family. 
-ability to message multiple people at once
-family and client ability to remain updated on status and keep all involved in the loop consistently 
-family ability to ask questions, send messages, add items to the calendar, etc. it promotes transparency among family, client and care team
-ability to use calendar to schedule staff and appointments. Also able to assign staff to tasks and ask for volunteer from family at times there is no staff in the home

Cons:
-friends can see most of what the inner circle sees. This poses a privacy issue for those not given authorization to see medical and clinical details. I have had to minimize information shared and can’t fully use the app in one of my cases
-inability to archive closed cases for future reference. They can only be deleted
-the care plan is only good for one day then disappears. From an agency perspective this limits our ability to do quality assurance and track trends
-notifications to email only link to the site but not the actual action it is notifying about so it takes extra time to locate what has been added
-inability to retract a message or edit
-support is quick to respond and helpful. However when I asked to whom I could direct my recommendations to I got no response. I’m hoping this review may get into the proper hands to address some of these suggestions for improvements 

Despite the “cons”,  have adopted used of this app for all of my clients receiving in-home care and feel it meets most of our needs.

text: Great site to share care plan, documents, contacts, calendar and more. It’s perfect for us 5 siblings to coordinate care for our dad. Biggest issue is “friends” and “inner circle” can see almost everything. I was going to upload my dad’s medical cards, Medicare Card, etc, but realized friends and inner circle can see them as well. I find this very intrusive. There’s absolutely no need for anyone else to see private documents. Therefore, the cousins we invited had to be cancelled or revoked. My advice to the developers is to allow the administrators to pick and choose categories for each group type to see. For example, friends can only read Wellness Journal, and inner circle can see that plus a couple other categories such as meds, calendar, messages. Until this happens, we’re just keeping this between the siblings.

title: Great idea

title: Terrible Experience
text:
I have a Galaxy Watch Series 3 and it doesn’t work very well with iOS.

First off, the "find phone" function is next to useless - it plays a very quiet sound and the option on the watch almost always seems to be greyed out. Turns out it requires the Galaxy Watch app to be running in the background, which is almost never the case even though I have background app refresh enabled. It seems to rely on media volume rather than ringtone volume, and I usually keep the media volume low.

Secondly, I hate how Weather, Store, and other apps rely on having a constant connection to your phone even when their function could reasonably be done over WiFi. It wasn't like this before - I used to be able to use these apps on WiFi just fine. Now they demand a connection to my phone constantly.

Finally, while this isn't a problem with the app (as far as I know), the watch once randomly decided to reset itself. It just said "Watch will be reset" and just wiped itself with no indication as to what triggered the reset. I don't know why or how it did this. A web search only revealed other users confused by a similar problem. The only thing I could find was some guy claiming it happens if you press the power button a bunch of times, but I didn't press power (if I did, it's way too easy to accidentally trigger.)

The only thing that has been consistently reliable is notifications - I've never missed a notification with the watch connected.

title: Better than Are You Dead App
text: I tried the Are You Dead app first but it was as gruesome as its name. I deleted that app but didn’t know to delete my emergency contacts first. So they started getting daily notices I hadn’t checked in. Getting that fixed was a nightmare because the app’s customer service was not responsive to my first five pleas for help. In contrast, I had response in a couple of hours to a question I had about this app and I love its sunny landing screen, upbeat language, and the daily inspiring quote. After thought, I opted for the paid version to have the phone calls from Snug operators first, before my emergency contacts are notified that I’ve missed a check-in. I also like that Snug can notify my local emergency responders. Both paid and free versions act if you miss one check-in, versus Are You Dead, which waits until you miss two check-ins. I want quicker help for my dog if I’m unresponsive. Finally, if you do the math, the cost of the paid version is 50 cents or so a day. I’m now forgetting the cost: it’s above $100. The daily cost is worth it for the peace of mind I receive in return.

title: Wonderful Service for Those Living Alone
text:
I am retired, live alone and have health issues, but am still able to care for myself. But I have nobody regularly checking on me. I am very busy, but my hobbies and pastimes tend to be done indoors, so neighbors are used to not seeing me outside for days at a stretch. Therefore, if I should ever fall or not be able to phone for help for any reason (Heaven forbid!), nobody would “miss me” for a long while. There are regular texts between me and several close relatives, but even they would not think anything was wrong if a week went by without hearing from me for a “catch-up.”
So - Enter SNUG!  What a wonderful service ( and the Basic Plan, which is all I need at present, is so helpful, easy-to-use, and FREE). I just set the alarm on my phone for a few
minutes before the daily check-on time I have given Snug. At this chosen time, I open my Snug App, check the box and immediately receive a cheery message on the same screen, saying I’m good for another day! 
And if I DON’T check the box within a few minutes, Snug notifies the back-up person I have provided, who will then check on me . 
So convenient, comforting and easy-peasy to use!

title: A great use of technology

All 3 of them got a text stating I had not checked in. It gives my children some “peace of mind”.  To me that is worth the effort to respond to a Snug text with one click every morning - or at what ever time one has set up. I have only the free part of the app so that is the only portion I am reviewing. This meets my needs in an excellent manner. I have not used the portion of the app that involves the paid actions. I am very active in a retirement community with lots of interaction with neighbors, friends and activities so this meets my needs well. But for people who are more isolated or at greater risk for adverse events, the paid actions of the app most likely would be of greater benefit. 
“Peace of Mind” is a great gift to give yourself as well as give to your children who worry about us!

title: Suggested Improvements
text: This app has a useful concept, but the check-in system needs better logic. I’ve had multiple false alerts simply because my phone battery died or the device was turned off, which causes unnecessary notifications to my contacts. For an app focused on safety, that is a real issue, especially for anyone using the paid plan that may escalate to calls or authorities. The app should use passive signals like phone movement, background activity, charging events, or detecting a reboot to tell the difference between a missed check-in and an actual problem. A toggle for daily health tips instead of pithy quotes would also make the check-in screen more relevant. With these changes, the app would avoid many needless alerts.

NOTE :: I LIVE ALONE AND TRIED ALL TYPES OF WAYS TO CHECK IN WITH FAMILY MEMBERS WHICH 
IS GOOD , BUT IT REALLY DOES NOT WORK WELL AT ALL , SO SNUG IS THE ANSWER FOR ALL TO STAY CONNECTED SO YOU ARE NOT IN DIRE SITUATIONS WITHOUT GOOD CONTACT HELP !!!!

title: My new little friend
text: A nice little smiling face to greet me every morning, check that I’m OK and give me words to live by - what could be better? Love it!

title: Useful app
text: As an older person whose circle of friends has shrunk I found this app very useful in assuring myself that if something happens to me and I don’t check in someone will be notified

title: A MUST for singles!
text: Being a live-alone, 78-yrs woman, I deeply appreciate the convenience of Snug.  And, my emergency contact has Snug entered on her phone if I fail to check-in with Snug each day.

title: Great App
text: This is a great app for people like me who live alone and appreciate a safety net in case they are ill or injured. It becomes an easy habit to check in every morning. I’ve used Snug for 8 months now and have never forgotten to connect.

title: Best free option
text: Most apps like this charge monthly fees, this one is free and works great! Great for someone who lives alone.

title: Nice app
text: Great app for peace of mind.  Easy to check in each day and you get several reminders to do so.  Wish the pay feature was a little cheaper.

title: Makes Me Feel Better, Safer
text: Now that I'm approaching my mid-seventies (yikes!!!) I need to become a bit more formal about my safety.  I'm in good shape and have people I can call but still "things happen".  This little Snug app is absolutely perfect for this time in my life, it just makes me feel a lot safer.  Later I may get more features but for now I like it a lot!

title: My daily check in
text: This app is truly amazing, and notifies me to check in every day, I use the basic features but you can get more features for a fee, it will let a family member or friend whoever you appointed to know if there if there might be an emergency if you do not check.

title: Thank you snug!
text: I hope you know how much comfort and kindness you have spread out into the world.

title: No more fear
text:
Senior living alone with no family close by to check on her created a fear. 
Snug freed me, so I now live fully.

title: Critical for anyone who lives alone
text:
I don’t care what age you are, this is the perfect way to make sure someone gets notified if you don’t hit the “deadman’s switch” once per day.  My biggest fear has always been that no one would know if I was injured or fell down stairs or whatever. Now someone will check in with me if I don’t click the check box every day.  

And that big check mark each morning makes me feel as if I’ve accomplished something!

title: Alone in the woods
text: Living alone in a remote area in my 60's, this brings me peace of mind. Help will be coming if I fail to check in at the next check-in time.

title: Peace of Mind
text: Living alone as a senior with disabilities, I greatly appreciate this app as a notification system for my family and friends. Thank you, Snug!!

title: ..happened again
text: It is 8am and the app just had me check in for 9pm so I don’t have to check in again until 8am in the morning lord forbid anything happen from now until then y’all really need to fix this it’s actually ridiculous and defeats the entire purpose of the app. It makes me want to find a new app to use I’ve already said this three or four times no one has fixed it I’m not going to keep threatening to leave I’m just going to do it next time. Maybe then you all when get someone on this extreme problem with the app.

title: Multiple daily check ins
text: I love the app!  It could be life saving for someone that lives alone.  I believe an option to schedule multiple check ins (at least 2) would be very useful. It could make a difference between life or death for someone with a busy family that doesn’t always call to check on them every day.

title: Live alone more safely at no charge!
text: I live alone and I appreciate Snug so much! You can adjust to your own settings on mine if I don’t check in by 7 o’clock snug notifies the contacts I have listed. It’s great knowing that if something happens to me, those closest to me will know. You also get an inspiring quote for the day and it’s free!

title: I like it!
text: Great App for those who don’t want to lose their independence

title: Piece of mind
text: Happy to got it recommended by my friend , makes me not to worry of living alone .

title: Peace of mind
text: So easy and great way to give family peace of mind without being intrusive and calling every day.

title: Snug As a Bug
text: I recently lost my wife and live by myself and have a history of seizures. My family was concerned and I too if something happens to me no one would find out. I found this app. Easy to use. Have my emergency contact set up which is easy to. It works because I lost my phone my sister got the notification I hadn’t checked in.  After being able to reach me she called for a wellness check paramedics showed up asking if I was ok. So the app works. They give you a couple of opportunities to check in if you miss you designated time. App is user friendly and can help a lot of people living around

title: Works great
text: I would find it more convenient to also have it available on my Apple Watch.

title: Great app to have, especially when you live alone!
text: I’m a single parent of a special needs child who wouldn’t be able to call for help if, god forbid, something happened to me overnight. Using Snug for check ins as soon as I wake up has brought me SO much peace of mind. I also made my mom who lives alone download/use it as well! Snug is so simple to use and can be paused at will for vacations and such. Fantastic app.

title: Easy to use app
text: Easy to use app and exactly what I needed For my safety and well being

title: Live alone? Get this app!
text: Great little app to let family and friends know that you are OK. Just click each morning and they’ll get a notification that you are up and about.

title: Easy peazy
text: Just a quick tap each morning when they remind you and you’re done. Love it.

title: Lifesaver
text: Has brought so much peace to my life.

title: Security
text: Always feel secure and help available when needed,

title: It really works
text:
As a pet sitter and a single person I appreciate Snug having my back. I had gotten busy one evening and forgot to check in. Even though the app did its part by sending me text messages reminding me I had not yet checked in. I didn’t hear them. Within maybe 10 to 15 minutes later my phone was blowing up from my contacts making sure I was ok. It was an unintentional test of the system and it worked perfectly. All 5 contacts were notified and all did their part to make sure I was ok. 
Thank you Snug.

title: Life saving app.
text: I started using this app 3-4 months ago.  I had been looking for an app that would make me feel more secure as a middle-aged woman who lives alone.  There are times where I go days and weeks without speaking to a family member or friend.  I also work from home, and I have multiple pets.  The thought of me dropping dead for some random reason, and then my dogs subsequently starving to death, or whatever other ungodly things that take place when someone passes at home alone, etc…  But, now, I have this handy dandy app that I check in with every day.  And, if I don’t check in, my emergency contacts will get a text message from the app to inform them I’ve gone rogue.  I feel exponentially “safer” knowing I have this fail proof, back up system that ensures someone will be notified to come and check on my and my animals.  The app also sends multiple reminders so that you don’t forget to check in.  At any rate, I highly recommend this app.  It’s incredibly easy to use, and it gives me a peace of mind that I would not have otherwise.  Thanks, Snug!!!

title: Provides Mental Comfort
text: While unexpectedly living alone now, this app provides a level of connection and safety.

title: Feels good
text: It does feel good to know someone is looking out for me- I know I must reach out each morning or my emergency contacts are texted. One morning I did forget and my sister called me- so I know this works! And I love the daily inspiration… I look forward to those quotes.

title: A life saving app
text: This app calls for help in your time of need or emergency. A must for those living alone.

title: Love snug!
text: I have been using Snug for years now.  It gives me a feeling of security.  I have accidentally proven how it works twice when they reached out to my contact person.  I tell all my friends about it!!

title: Exceptional service!
text: I have been using SNUG for about six years and rely on it for my safety.  It gives me peace of mind! I live alone, and this service is invaluable!  I highly recommend Snug.

title: Thankful for Snug
text: This is my fourth year using Snug. It is a much needed app and a wonderful solution for people living alone. It gives a sense of security and puts one at ease knowing that if you don’t check in someone will be contacted. Thank you Snug for following through on a brilliant idea.

title: Great idea!
text: As an “elderly” person living alone, this gives me peace of mind for my dog (and me). If I can’t check in or get to the phone, at least someone will know to check up on me.

title: EVERYONE living alone should have Snug Safety
text: When I became a widow living alone, I realized that nobody would know if I woke up every morning. It's a terrible but very real thing to consider. And it's not dependent on age, it's about living alone in a world where people are busy and cannot be expected to check on their friends and relatives daily. SNUG is an absolute blessing and the perfect solution. It works flawlessly and I tell all my doctors about it for the benefit of their patients.

title: Works sporadically
text:
I did a few tests.  The first one waited an hour before it contacted my emergency contact. 
Also per snug it only checks location every 4 hours. So, depending on what time you have your check in set for, it may never have your correct location.   It sent my emergency contacts the incorrect location.  Good thing we already have life360!

title: Disappointed
text: Not a smart app.  Short notice period before emergency notification.  Does not reset daily and no notices are sent until a check in.  I’ve gone four days without a check in. Price is also very expensive.

title: Redhead
text: The app gives my daughter the security that I am ok without us having to make a phone call when it’s not convenient maybe .

title: Some days it texts me and some days it doesn’t.
text: I liked it when it would texts me and tell me somebody checked in. It seems to do that sporadically. Email notifications may or may not work since I get hundreds of emails in the day and because of time differences it could be hours before I get to an email from SNUG. It would be helpful if that was a permanent option. I could get a whole BUNCH more people to join (for you to mine their data too) if that was an option.  Com’on, when a product is free, we know we’re the product- and I’m okay with that if it functioned in a more efficient way.

title: Great idea for an app
text: Great idea to make sure my elderly parents check-in daily. Also great for me as a single person. Thanks Snug Safety!

title: Peace of mind
text: My  husband has been passed away 2 1/2 years ago , and for the first time in 50 years, I was alone! At the time I had no idea what all of that would come to mean, but I have learned that Security is one of the precious commodities when you are alone. A friend told me about the Snug app and since I have been using this app , I can rest assured that somebody will help me in a time of a health crisis., As one living alone. I have dedicated three people as my “go to.” individuals to check in on me if I do not check in every morning. It gives me confidence that although I am living alone, this is just one way to help assure that I can continue to do so. And the cherry on the top of the cake is that it is also a free app. I could not be happier. And I have told all of my single friends about this app. Many of them are enjoying it just as I am. … it’s absolutely the best thing.thank you snug !

title: Good idea for the elderly that live alone.
text: I see this as a binary condition dead or alive. I don’t want to be found after days of an accident where nobody has come to feed my cats. That’s pretty much it.

title: Relief

Highly recommend this app for anyone living solo.

This seems like a great safety net until my kids are old enough to learn how to call for help. I only left off a star because I’d like to have the option to set more than one check in time per day - morning and afternoon.

title: LOVE IT!!!
text: I truly cannot recommend this app enough! If you are the sole caregiver for someone who would be unable to alert authorities if something happened to you, please for the sake of their safety, get this app. It has given me so much peace of mind knowing that someone would be alerted to come help my toddler immediately after I missed a check-in. I’ve just forgotten to check in before and a live dispatch agent has called and called my emergency contacts. I was okay but so good to know it works! This really gives so much peace of mind!

text: My girlfriend told me about this app because I live by myself and I don’t always talk to the same people every day. So I have three of my family members on as my contacts if I don’t check into Snug. It gives me security that if something happened they would find me relatively soon versus if I didn’t have this app. Love love love SNUG!

title: Love this app
text: I live by myself and am 71 years old.  I was afraid that if something happened to me that no one would know for days.  I remembered when my mom was alive she had paid for an account that she could check in daily.  So I started my search for something similar.  I found Snug and was delighted to find there was a free option.  I signed up immediately and put my kids as the people who would be notified.  When my youngest child saw this they also decided to sign up since they live alone.  Have been using this app now for a few months and it’s easy.  If you want to sign up for a phone call you can for a small fee.  Definitely recommend.

title: Remind me

title: I love snug

title: Super useful

I think this app could be very helpful for folks living alone. I have not used the paid features yet.
Good job, Snug!

title: Useful app!
text: Very simple and easy to use phone app that requires no additional equipment (watches, bracelets, clip-ons); just your mobile phone.  The free version works well for me at this time but will eventually switch over to the paid version which has excellent enhanced features.

title: Helpful if u live alone

title: Keeps privacy
text: My children worry that I have no one to check up on me. Snug check-in gives them the knowledge I'm okay so they don't have to call or drop by to check on me. THANKS SNUG.

title: Better Than A Phone Chain..and a real good idea.
text:
Help! I’ve fallen and can’t get up!

Oh my God, what will happen to me? No one knows. I live alone. What will my pets do? 

This is a real concern as people age. Wait, you’ll find out. I have. 

I used to have the Help I’ve fallen kit, and all the hardware and necklaces. And a big bill. 

I considered starting a phone chain and calling friends each day to check in. Intrusive. Cumbersome. Time consuming. 

So I found the SNUG app. Inexpensive. Add three trusted people. Check in once a day with SNUG by opening the app and hitting a button. 

Fail to, and SNUG will CALL YOU. Fail to answer SNUG will call your contacts and then 911 if it is a real emergency. 

A very useful app.

title: Love the APP
text:
UPDATE:I received the help I needed to get back into the app. While SNUG was in my contacts, the actual phone number was blocked. Not sure how that happened. Once unblocked I was able to receive the verification code and log back in.  Still the best and easiest app for single, elderly, disabled, college kids or similar to use and let family or friends know your safe without being intrusive. 

The app is simple and easy!! The reason I will NOT give it 5 stars is due to their customer service!!! If you ever get a new phone (same number) you need to re login and in order to do that you in put your number and wait for a code to enter. The problem is you will NEVER  get that code!!! So obviously the next step is to call but they will NEVER answer the phone and you have to leave a message. They will NEVER return your call. At this point the only way to check in is to call them and do the automated check in. Now you have to find their website   (Snugsafety.com…you’re welcome) and email support expressing your issue. At some point you’ll get a response with a code that lasts 10 mins or so, but since you aren’t attached to email that code will expire and not work. Do you see where I’m going with this? They have  lousy customer service!! It’s been this way since I’ve started using this app many years ago! I doubt they’ll ever make a change, but if you can suffer through those issues, the app itself is great! Still waiting for my code!!!!

title: Absolute do NOT recommend
text: I was initially excited about this app due to its simple check-in process and helpful reminders. However, only one of my emergency contacts received a notification to start receiving alerts if I miss a check-in. Despite following Snug support’s advice to delete and re-add contacts or switch to email notifications, my non-tech-savvy emergency contacts still haven’t received any notifications. What was supposed to be an easy safety solution has turned into a frustrating and unreliable experience.

title: A Life-Style Saver
text: The Snug app has been a real gift for me. I wanted some sort of daily check-in system but didn’t want to bother anyone with texting or calling, so Snug is absolutely perfect for me. Just a quick tap on the phone and all is well. I also like getting several reminders, especially in the early going before it became a part of my daily routine. I don’t recall the name of the lady who created this app, but I’m very grateful for it.

title: And Snug is like a hug
text: At 66 yrs old Iam an orphan , no family or children . I do have a Church family & I have listed my wonderful brother in Christ my Pastor Chuck as my person, I know if I do not check in He will be here for me, calling & if need be coming to my door. I dont worry about me but I do worry for my lil dog as it could be 2 weeks before anyone would notice me missing & I just couldnt bear my lil baby to suffer. Thanks to Snug I no longer worry .

title: I love Snug
text: It’s very reliable and makes me feel safe.

title: Snug Safety Check-in Daily
text:
I have been using Snug since my new senior housing facility did not have much of an emergency 🆘, and inquired on Google for something to fit the bill so to speak.  I found this app on the Apple App Store and felt it would handle what I was concerned about.  ‘Let me tell you, it does’.  I one time forgot (in the beginning) to check in (I have the premium service @ $99/yr), and I have my brother listed as a Contact person.  They called him, he called me, they called me, would call 911 shortly if I didnt respond NOW!  My Time Limit was set at 12 Noon, I reported in at 12:02pm.  So, I now have changed from 00:01-11:59am to check in daily, to 00:01-13:30, or 12:01am to 1:30pm daily.  I now check in mostly mid mornings.  
It’s good to have, works in all of contiguous 48 states, where ever your cell phone is located.  BTW, age 84 and now a widower.

title: Live Alone
text: I live alone and don’t have anyone to call in an emergency. Snug makes me feel that someone is looking out for me if I have a problem.

title: Peace of mind
text: Living alone has its challenges. Now that I have Snug, there are a few fewer worries in my life. I appreciate the peace of mind. I have knowing that if I don’t check in, someone will check on me.

title: Loving it
text: I live alone and my love ones are a distance away from me. I don’t drive and I feel so isolated. If something were to happen to me who would know? The snug app gives me a chance to prove I’m alive. The response makes me feel as though someone is watching out for me and watching for my signal. It is indeed reassuring. My mood is so much better just from having this app. I love it. My family loves it as well. They have a chaotic schedule (to me) and tell me how reassured they are about my safety and condition. Thanks Snug.

title: Great check in for people living alone
text: I live alone and am older and no one else checks in on me.  All too busy to remember.  So I feel more secure with Snug.  It works great. Nice quote of the day too .

title: Easy to Use
text: Easy to use and peace of mind for me and for my loved ones.

title: Snug, my daily pal!
text: I have been using Snug for more than three years now. I look forward to the daily quote each morning, even if it’s a rerun. Snug gives me a sense of security, since I live alone. I have tested it multiple times, usually on purpose, but sometimes by forgetting to check in. it has always notified my contacts when I don’t check in on time.

title: Safety and awareness
text: It’s very beneficial for me to check in on a daily basis as it keeps me on track to make sure I’m okay every morning. My major concern, and it doesn’t have anything to do with Snug, is that if I don’t respond, I don’t have someone to check on me on a timely basis. The person who is my contact doesn’t make the effort to check on me if I don’t respond. She rarely, if ever, responds to anyone quickly. She’s always more involved in her own life (self, family, and then friends). If I don’t respond, I’d appreciate it if Snug could/would contact a call center or emergency personnel to make sure I’m okay. I’ve never needed someone to be contacted, but just in case. I don’t have any family and very few close friends.

title: Peace of mind
text: So your family will always know you’re still alive and doing well. Hopefully there’s the Snug app to keep them alerted, even though you live alone that you were still around and they do not have to worry about you another day day by day you will love this app more and more I highly recommend it and it’s free, thank you dear God for whoever invented this app and let God bless them.

title: Perfect

title: Great, easy app

title: Mr Pete
text:
Snug is FANTASTIC app that I’m thrilled with. This is one of a very few app reviews I have ever written. I would rate it much higher if it were possible. I am using the free version which fits my needs perfectly.

Having done that, she’s trapped if something happens to me at night. Snug lets me add our daughter and her husband as emergency contacts to be notified if I fail to “check in” at a preset time. I verified within the app that the time zone was changed to HST and was no longer set on PST. I left the check-in time limit set at 10:00 every morning. However, the app began notifying me three hours too early at 4 a.m. that it was time to check in. At 6 a few mornings I got the warning message asking me if I was OK. And then one morning I slept late and it called my contacts at 7 a.m. It is three hours earlier in Hawai’i. The app does not recognize changes in the time zone - even when set to a new time zone. I did send screenshots of this issue to SNUG support but did not receive a resolution. Maybe in the next update?

title: BP Notes History & Add Notes Disappeared!
text:
I have been using this app for over 3 years. I have been in a hypertensive crisis for the past 4 weeks and have been faithfully tracking my BP WITH NOTES for context for my doctor who is using the readings AND NOTES to tweak and adjust my BP med dosages and parameters. Now I can no longer see my notes history, nor does the app have the Add Note or Edit Note features anymore! 

Why in the world would you eliminate such important features from this app?! I have literally been using this app and my Omron wrist cuff to get through a terribly frightening crisis, and I wake up today to the app that took away one of its most important features for my use of it! Now THAT will raise a patient’s BP even more! 

The app is useless if I have to document contextual notes elsewhere in another app (like a Notes app) per BP reading. It is stressful enough to be in the midst of medically trying to stabilize and regulate my BP again, and now I have lost the ease of documenting in-the-moment notes all in one place. 

As a software engineer myself, this change in usability is completely unacceptable for the user and renders the app essentially unusable for the purposes I have stated in this review. I cannot tell you how disappointed and upset I am at this removal of functionality!

title: Locked out of my own data with no way to fix it
text:

I tried to update. The App Store tells me the app is "currently not available in your country or region." I'm in the United States, and the app's own sign-in screen has United States selected.

So the app demands an update that the App Store won't let me download. I can't view my blood pressure history, and I can't sync new readings from my Omron monitor. There's no link to support, no explanation, and no workaround offered in the app.

Omron, please either restore the app's availability in the US App Store or let the current version read existing data. People use this to track health readings for their doctors, and being locked out with no path forward isn't acceptable.

title: New app change. Can’t edit errant readings!
text:
On 9/29/2026 the developer sent me this message not realizing they had already made the readings editable again. What bunch of buffoons:

We appreciate you sharing your thoughts about the recent changes to the app, especially regarding the inability to edit readings. It’s understandable how this impacts your experience, particularly when dealing with mixed readings. Your feedback about the wrist cuff's accuracy and the need for flexibility in managing data is invaluable, and we’ve flagged this internally for further consideration. While


Looks like OMRON returned to editing readings - for now 


OMRON has removed the ability to edit errant readings which is a brutally bad idea. 

My wife got her readings mixed in with mine and I can’t edit them out. Some OMRON corporate nonsense about “data integrity”. 

Other issues are  that this wrist cuff can give wildly errant readings that require repeat testing to get 2 or 3 in a row that are close then I (used to) save the mean reading. 

Also, when I repeat the test on the other wrist when it’s wildly wrong on the wrist,  I used to repeat the opposite wrist reading 1 minute later until I get 3 accurate readings on a row. 

But now the bad readings are locked in place on the app which is BS. 

I don’t care about Omron’s “data integrity” nonsense because their data by definition lacks integrity because their wrist cuffs are a POS.

I care about knowing my readings are accurate and Omron deciding to lock the data is really annoying. 

I’m either dumping OMRON and buying a more accurate upper arm cuff that allows for error edit or I’m just deleting their app completely and keeping the readings manually. 

Renpho BP cuffs allow for deletions. 

I’m looking into buying one of those and tossing the OMRON in the trash.

title: New Update Makes Adding Notes Painfully Slow Since 8.5.0
text:
I’ve been using the Omron app for a long time, and the usability took a major step backward starting with version 8.5.0. The “New Home Screen” update introduced a workflow change that makes adding notes significantly more difficult than before.

Previously, I could add a note directly from the main screen. Now, when I tap a reading, the app takes about 10 seconds to load — and it always loads the chart first. I don’t need the chart, and I don’t use the chart for adding notes, yet I’m forced to see it every single time I want to annotate a reading. After that delay, I have to scroll down to “See all measurements,” but the scrolling is laggy and often requires several swipes before the app responds. Only after selecting “See all measurements” can I scroll again, enable “Show notes,” and finally add a note. This is a clear usability regression.

This change affected me during a medically sensitive moment. I was recently hospitalized for a stroke, and I rely on the ability to quickly annotate readings when symptoms or stress occur. The new slow, chart‑first workflow made it harder to document an important reading in real time, which is unacceptable for a health‑tracking app.

Omron should restore the ability to add notes directly from the main screen or streamline the workflow. Users who depend on this app for real medical situations should not be forced to wait through delays, laggy scrolling, and an unnecessary chart just to record essential information.

If this workflow cannot be improved, I may need to switch to another app that supports my Omron monitor, because quick note‑taking is essential for my medical tracking.

title: Absolutely love my Gear Fit2 Pro & this app but have questions
text:
**UPDATED**
My husband bought me the watch a few years ago.  In over 30 years of marriage definitely one of his best choices!  At that time I used the Android app on my LG K20 VS501; despite what many have reported I never experienced any problems even while using Bluetooth headphones.
The Android app allowed me to access music from my phone directly from the app while using the exercise tab for tracking walking.  Additionally, I was able to receive distance, speed, pace etc. cues audibly which I could set through my settings.  That feature was a big help!
Fast forward:  last summer I moved into the iPhone XR.  I set everything up with the Apple apps.  Connects easily every time, & this app also allows for easy syncing.  At first I drove myself crazy trying to find my 2 favorite features:  the music icon & audible cues.  At first I thought the cues were just not coming through my headset but after trying it without headphones I discovered there were none, only countdown.  (Countdown also does not come through Bluetooth headset.). I even switched to the running tab, thinking the option would be there; nothing.  Yes, I tried without music:  no more nice fellow voice to encourage me.
Although the missing link to my music can be worked around I really miss the audible cues.  Am I missing something as to how to find such setup ( which was easy in Android)?  Is there a reason why those features are not in the app for Apple?
**Finally, one additional question:  although I have my step count set to be from my watch exclusively with the app (all shows correctly!) since my phone is not tied to my hip the integration with Apple’s Health app only shows my phone’s step count.  Why does the app’s step count not utilize my choice of source when combined with the health app?  I use the Health app to integrate with rewards for healthy living from Walgreens & AARP.
Thank you!

***Nice quick response***
It is a rare instance where a developer offers a response so quickly!  Thank You!
Just to clarify, I already have my step count source set to my Gear Fit2 Pro.  (For anyone working off reviews, the developer’s response is an excellent demonstration how to do such if you do not know how to select!)
My steps always record from my watch, syncing each time I open my SHealth app.  My daily goal is always in my view, one way or another.
I guess what I am asking is, although my watch step count is correct in the SHealth app, why does my Apple Health app only show my phone’s step count (as opposed to my selected step count source properly recorded)?  Yes, they are linked with SHealth being a data source allowing Apple Health to read.  I have tried entering the difference in steps manually but it never saves. 
Thank you, again! 
STAY SAFE EVERYONE & PLEASE keep Social Distancing!

Fitbit shows calorie intake and calories burned and they calculate for you weather or not you have burned enough calories to stay in a certain range. To me that is a great incentive to be a little more active when I can see if I have burned enough calories to have a snack and still maintain a caloric deficit. And it isn’t just as simple as setting a calorie intake goal for the day. If I tell Fitbit I want to stay 200 intake calories below my calories burned it just adjusts throughout the day. If I have been more active it allows me to consume more. Also Fitbit has a very nice UPC (barcode) scanner option for when you are logging what you are eating. I have not found that in the Samsung Health app. Lastly I would like to have the ability to customize the three main focus points on the Home Screen. I am not interested in my sleep patterns so I would much rather replace that with a calories burned tile.

text:
Some friends have Androids, some have iPhones. A bunch of them were already using Samsung Health, so we wanted to see if we could integrate and compete on steps during the week. Unfortunately iPhone users are not allowed to join step challenges with android users. Okay, fine.

But then we realized you can add friends to your leaderboard, regardless of platform, which is a huge win. Now though we can't do challenges together, we can use the leaderboard to informally compete over the 7 day rolling week. We are all fine with this.

Except we just realized for the iPhone folks, Samsung Health ONLY pulls steps from the iPhone itself as the data source, meaning that Apple Watch steps are not tracked at all. Despite the fact that I even disabled step tracking on the phone itself, and prioritized the Apple Watch in Apple Health as the #1 data source for step tracking, Samsung Health will not pull any steps at all unless they are from the iPhone. I was a little set off about it seemed like I was being hounded but after talking with the nice lady by chat I decided to talk to her. She is trying to help people understand how to use the app. Walked me thru how to test it and made sure I didn’t have any questions. The only problem I found was the seizure alarm went off when I wasn’t even monitoring. It would send alerts to my husband and daughter while they were at work and of course they would freak out. I immediately told them it was a false alarm. Once is ok but it happened several times during the day. If I ended up needing help they would be so used to false alarms they may not take it seriously and where does that leave me ? My watch was on the nightstand last night and I noticed the green light that is usually up against your arm was glowing. I picked up the watch and it immediately set off another alarm. I’ve since learned I needed to log out of the app on my phone for it to shut off on my watch. It was such a mess yesterday that I’ve deleted the app off my phone completely. The whole idea of an app to help you when your in desperate need is a good one but needs some work. Or maybe I do ? Just doesn’t work for me. And now I’m wondering if I will be charged for the call I received from Australia to set it up ? That will not make me very happy.

text: Offers simple interface with voice commands. Biggest advantage over other fall detection apps is that it identifies the type of fall and contacts the right type of help. title: Something changed
text:
When I first set up my CaringBridge account I was impressed and looking forward to using it. But it is no longer user-friendly.

If you look at other less-than-stellar reviews, you’ll notice that they’re not really reviews. They’re requests for help. The company replies to these by telling people to ask for help via their help page. 

Unfortunately, their help page is practically useless. It fails to answer the simplest questions. Using their chat feature is a waste of time, since it doesn’t understand the most basic questions. After a couple of tries, it says it is turning you over to a human. 

Alas, if you’re super unlucky, it tells you no humans are available, but they’ll contact you by email to help that way. That’s better than nothing, but by the time you’ve spent an hour struggling with the app, then struggling with the “help”, you might be pretty aggravated. 

That seems counterproductive for an app that’s supposed to make my life easier while I cope with a life-threatening illness.

Now that I’ve written all that, I’m lowering the rating from three stars to two. The only reason it’s not one star is because I’m holding onto hope that the app will become user friendly and helpful again.

Note to CaringBridge: If you respond to this by telling me to go to your help section, I’ll probably cry.

title: Helpful App - Sharing on iPad Not Working
text:
CaringBridge is a wonderful service and we appreciate it so much, especially in this time when our family has a member who has a life-changing medical condition. I offer this feedback as an opportunity for improvement and not a judgment.

When I share an update on my iPhone, the full action dialogue opens with all options available. On my iPad, I am presented with a tooltip and only the action dialogue header with the name of the app appears with no actions. I have looked to see if there is an option I have not enabled, but I can find none. I believe it may be a bug due to the tooltip container.

One other issue is that the app freezes in an auto-save mode which never resolves. I have to copy any content to the pasteboard or another app and force-quit. Once relaunched, there seems to be a window of time before it happens again. I paste the content and send before that happens usually. If I am interrupted, which can happen frequently for a caregiver, the issue reoccurs.

We are grateful for this app and this service. Thank you.

title: Your website is more and more annoying!!!
text:
Update to my earlier comments:
Since posting the review below, I have received daily, repetitive emails from Apple that have the same response from the developer of Caring Bridge. So far, 10 identical emails. The emails invite me to update my review. And each one has the same auto-generated comment from CB. I chalk up this repetition to just another software glitch on the CB side. Meanwhile, I’ve also read through many comments on the site posted by other people. I see I am not alone. Many complaints about the flow of the website, notifications not working, and too many requests for donations. And that same generic message gets repeated on most of these reviews. 

My original message:
I have notifications set up so that I know when there is a new update from friends whose serious illness I am worried about. But first, I have to plow through your asks for a donation on every visit to the site. Even though I recently GAVE money to Caring Bridge. And I get more and more fundraising asks by notification. These are NOT the notifications I have agreed to. Now I feel I must remove all notifications, which means I may miss important information about my friends!

title: Review of CaringBridge
text:
I just had successful kidney transplant surgery at Mayo. 
I have had five years of FSGS, two and a half years of dialysis and three people trying to donate a kidney but being unable to due to health reasons. Literally hundreds of people have been praying for us, some I’ve never met!
Once we got the call and we were hustling to get from Greenville SC to Mayo in Minnesota ASAP the CaringBridge site provided the most effective and efficient way to communicate with anyone who desired information and updates. 
It has been a whirlwind week. My recovery is ahead of schedule and my doctors are all pleased. 
FIVE STARS AND THANK YOU CARINGBRIDGE!! ❤️😇🎯
Joel and Ann Shaw
Greenville SC
June 12, 2024

title: This transition to the new format is beyond challenging
text: I wrote a Caring Bridge post this evening and posted it. Then I shared it with about a dozen friends who aren’t able to follow it online with a link sent via text. Some were apparently able to access it, but others weren’t. Ditto for those who read our posts online. We heard from a couple of people, but even my own husband just got a blank screen when he tried to read the post on Caring Bridge. At one point I finally realized that the instructions for sharing posts could only be followed on my computer, not on the mobile app. So I copied the link as instructed, but ran aground from not knowing how to send the copied link from my computer to my phone to send in a text message. This transition to the new Caring Bridge has meant running into one scary wall after another. It’s kind of sad that you aren’t able to staff a “help” phone line. That would help a great deal. Thanks for the wonderful service you have provided for us across these last years of our cancer journey. But I may have to look for some kind of alternative because our lives are stressful enough without the daily drama of wondering what the next challenge will be

title: What happened?
text:
I’ve authored and co-authored several CaringBridge sites over the years. I have appreciated the relative ease of creating, updating and otherwise modifying sites - until earlier this year. Don’t know what happened to blow CaringBridge out of the water a few months ago, and the complete lack of communication about it was baffling. I’d still appreciate something more than “we’re working hard.”

While there’s been progress in recent months, the site still lacks much of its previous usability. As an author, I find it clumsy, difficult, and frustrating to use. More importantly, large numbers of my sister’s supporters and readers have stopped using it, and that is a very great loss.

Are there plans to restore more functionality? Will CaringBridge communicate anything of substance that might help its users? Is anyone paying attention to feedback from the community of users? I hope so.

Thanks for your time and attention.

title: Peace of Mind for Families, Wherever You Are!
text:
My job involves frequent travel, and Life360 has been an invaluable app for keeping our family connected, no matter where we are in the world.

It gives us tremendous peace of mind knowing where our loved ones are at any given time. As parents, we particularly appreciate being able to see not only where our children are, but also how fast they are driving! It’s an excellent combination of convenience, connectivity, and family safety.

My only disappointment is that the Emergency Assistance feature isn’t supported in my country. If it were available, I wouldn’t hesitate for a moment to upgrade to the premium plan!

Overall, an outstanding app that I would highly recommend to families, especially those who travel frequently or have children who drive. Well done, Life360!

title: Worth the peace and protection
text:
I bought this app years ago and never realized how useful at the time it was going to be for my future.
First my son had his phone stolen on the bus and I went directly to the house to retrieve it back in less than an hour. 

Second, my husband was in another state for work and experienced an accident. The phone didn’t notify me of anything regarding the accident, but when I couldn’t find him I was able to use the Life360 app to tell me where he was and the phone was located inside a hospital. He was brought in as unknown without identification and if it wasn’t for the app putting me in the correct direction it could have been weeks to months or not at all that I was notified about my husband’s whereabouts. Because of the app I was able to find him within a day of him arriving to the hospital and was able to get him started on surgeries he needed.

I’ve kept the app ever since and it’s very reassuring to have for regular day to day.

I would recommend it and I use it daily.

title: On the fence so Deleted App
text:
Perhaps I missed something but I downloaded what I thought was a free app, only to find out that it is a 7-day free trial and a monthly subscription is required. Why? Is this something that recently changed? Is there something amiss? It also keeps prompting to give full access to certain features on my device after I have disallowed it. This is why I deleted the app. Additionally, the app requires access to A LOT of personal and device information and features (based on what is outlined in the privacy policy). I am not sure is actually necessary.

I understand that @Life360 is marketed and useful as a safety monitoring/tracking device, and it is. Although, I wish there was an actual free version with the same safety and monitoring the app was designed for (with the paid subscription providing the additional features it promotes) however, ALL the access it requires seems to align more with surveillance and what seems like less autonomy of your personal privacy and that of your family. I’ll need to understand more if I choose to download again.

title: Delayed Safety Notifications Defeat the Purpose of Life360
text:
What good is Life360 for parents if notifications that our children have arrived at or departed from a location can be delayed by 3–5 minutes? Parents rely on this app for safety, awareness, and peace of mind. A notification that arrives several minutes after our child has already left or arrived defeats the purpose of receiving that alert in the first place.

When it comes to our children’s safety, timing matters. Parents should not have to wonder whether their child has left school, arrived home, or reached another destination while waiting several minutes for Life360 to notify them.

Life360 needs to take this issue seriously. Location and arrival/departure notifications should be delivered as promptly as technically possible, with reliable background tracking and minimal delays. If there is a technical limitation causing these delays, the company needs to explain it clearly and address it.

Parents depend on this app for more than convenience. We depend on it for information that helps us look after our children. A family safety app should prioritize timely, reliable notifications. Please fix this issue.

text:
After noticing appointments are not staying on the app, I asked the Cozi support if there was a way to determine if someone is deleting the appointments or if they are falling off. Cozi’s response:
Cozi responded to your review of Cozi Family Organizer		
Cozi Family Organizer
Cozi
"Hi, We're sorry for any issues or concerns! Cozi doesn't offer a calendar tracking feature that would enable you to identify who in your account made changes to the calendar or when, and we've reiterated your request that we add this feature in the future. For now, though, any events that you add to the calendar with an online connection will remain in the calendar unless you or someone else in the account manually deletes them. There's no known reason for events that have been saved with an online connection to be deleted other than if someone in the account deletes them. We apologize again for any issues you're having, and if we can help further with this or with anything else please reach us again at cozi.com/contact-us so we can try to help further. Thanks, Cozi"

I confirm my appointments are saved in the app before I leave the office. title: Doesn’t play well with digital displays
text:
I’ve subscribed to Cozi Gold since 2017 and love it, but will be cancelling my account. We have a digital display (Mango Display) and for months Cozi worked great. In February there was an update causing all day events to start at either 11pm the day prior or 4am day of. On very, very rare occasions it displays the start time correctly for a very short amount of time, we are talking a few minutes every few days/ weeks if that. I’ve watched the display flip start times between 11pm the day prior, 4 am day of and the correct all day time within seconds. I reached out to Cozi and their response was the calendar links port into Google Calendar correctly so it isn’t a problem on their end. That instead of selecting all day, time it from 0000 - 2359. Yeah, no. Mango Display cannot find the error on their part. I’ve tried other calendar links with Mango Display and all day events are displayed correctly leading to the belief that it is a Cozi issue. I give up since Cozi is unwilling to try and figure out the error to correct it. To me, it isn’t worth the price since it doesn’t perform how I need it to.


Editing after developer response : 
I initially agreed with your reply that it was a Mango Display issue until I found others using different digital displays that were having the same issue!  If you do a google search, you will find posts from users of other platforms that have their all day events over multiple days due to start time. 
A work-around was adding my cozi calendar to my Google Calendar and having that sync with Mango Display. All day events displayed correctly in both Google Calendar and on my Mango Display. This brings me back to why am I paying for something that doesn’t work how I need it to and I’m using a free option to achieve my goal.

text:
I’ve had this app for about five years. Please listen to this if you plan to use this between your partner and you or your family as your new organization app.

It’s certainly better than having nothing, my partner and I have used it to keep track of our grocery list in real time. 

Before I get into the mini issues, just know that there are better apps. I’m gonna be switching everything over to AnyList. We will see how that goes.

It’s very often that the app has loading issues when everything else works perfectly fine. It’s often slow and when you need it to be in a rush, there’s always a pop-up asking you to upgrade. I suppose that can be pretty normal for a lot of free apps but it just adds to the annoyance when the loading is significantly longer than any other app. We keep having glitches in the system, where it deletes items off our list, or un checks already bought items, confusing the other person to buy things we don’t need. Recently it’s gotten very bad, hence why we were switching everything over. Sometimes we will go to check items off the list and in real time it clicks checked and then a second later clicks unchecked. Like it’s fighting against us to save the data we’re trying to put in. That’s a major issue for an app that is solely focused on real time responsive checking and the information that’s on that list. It puts us in a really tough spot if we’re already out at the store and we’re having a ton of issues with the app because it requires my partner to give me a call and make sure that the things that I put on the list are actually on the list by choice and not buy a glitch. title: Bring Back Fitbit
text:
The forced update to Google Health is an ABSOLUTE disaster and has made this app completely useless. 

It is a laughably ridiculous downgrade, and as a longtime user, I will sadly never purchase a Fitbit again if the app does not return to normal ASAP. 

The original Fitbit app was perfect, beautifully designed and the best on the market in terms of how elegant, simple, and efficient it was. Maybe I could get over the awful appearance of Google Health if the functionality stayed the same, but no. Not only is this garbage aesthetically childish and overwhelming, with huge neon bubbles and bold comic sans taking up the whole screen, it is SIGNIFICANTLY harder to use. It’s cluttered with hideous graphics and unnecessary new pages and sections hiding the most basic information??

Fitbit used to show all your info on ONE page (with the date), and you could click the arrows up top to see the overview from yesterday, for example, or select any day from the calendar and see all your stats (steps, calories burned, cardio load, distance, etc.) in ONE place with ONE click. Now, even this BASIC feature of a health app is gone. Nobody has time to go hunting within each and every stat bubble for their historical data when that is supposed to be the entire PURPOSE of the app. 

You’d think this would all be common sense at a $4 trillion tech company BEFORE this BS was forced on us, but even if not, it is now widely agreed upon among users. Please fix it.

TLDR; get any other fitness tracker because Google ruined a great app. 💔
