title: Optimized for slop
text:
I’ve used FitBit for years - I lost over 100 lbs using the food and exercise tracker but I’ve tried using it for months since the Google Health update and it’s unusable. 

1. Food Tracking - the database was never the best but you could make it work. Now try searching sweet potatoes to enter 100 grams. Nothing even resembling a plain uncooked sweet potato comes up let alone the USDA sweet potato calorie estimated comes up (a food in the USDA’s free foundational foods data source!) so I search roasted sweet potatoes and I get an entry for 1 unit.  Whats the unit? Unknown. Try and update it to grams. I cant update the number of grams because it added 205 units (?) and I can’t delete them. And that doesn’t even touch the confusion about whether the roast sweet potato entry includes the oil for cooking. 

2. Calorie deficit - They changed the calories deficient tracking from a hard deficit to a range - which I actually don’t mind. But I had to go to Reddit to figure out how to set a deficit because in the old app I could set my goal weight, current weight and the app would help me calculate my TDEE.  Now I have to use an outside TDEE calculator and the come back and set my calorie range.  Which is not clear at all and if I were just using the app I would assume by entering a goal weight it was giving me a correct calorie range. 

3.  AI slop - thankfully the app lets you turn off their AI coach so you don’t have to deal with that if you don’t want to. But I have to assume all of these changes are to force the user to use their AI and take pictures of their food to get calories and talk to their AI coach to get your true deficit so I find it high deceptive and gross.  Making a product worse isn’t changing people’s behavior to use it the way you want anymore - it’s just driving people away from the product.

title: Innacurate, and  downgrade from previous Fitbit app
text: I primarily use Fitbit for sleep tracking. My experience with the new app has been disappointing. The most notable problem with the app is its inaccuracy, but even the way data is presented is much less useful than offered in the original app. On my very first occasion using the app, after opening the old app and being required to download the new version I noticed that the total sleep reflected in the new app was 14 minutes higher than in the previous version of the app. The experience since that time has been similarly frustrating. For instance, I have come to learn that there are periods of time in which I have awakened before falling back asleep, and even periods of time in which I've gotten out of bed for several minutes before going back to bed and sleep, which are not reflected in the overall tracking of wakefulness over the course of a sleep session. For that reason total sleep time is, as previously mentioned, completely unreliable. Moreover, If the app isn't capable of measuring a change of state involving getting out of bed and walking around for 10 minutes before getting back into bed and going to sleep how can one rely on it making the far less certain discernment estimating a change in sleep from light to REM of deep, for example? I already had questions about Fitbit's accuracy when comparing it with an EEG measuring device I had previously used before that broke, but with the new Google Health app involved in the analysis I have it is clear that the way data is collected and measured is completely unreliable. Even the internal management and presentation of data is unacceptable. For instance, I have noticed that if I toggle between different detailed views for my daily sleep data in the app that the daily sleep score changes. Looking more closely I could see that other daily sleep metrics (such as total time asleep, and the length of different sleep stages) also changed, just by shifting views for a single, specific night. Beyond that problem the app can be confusing because it apparently defaults to weekly averages at times, so even when trying to navigate daily information one must sometimes reselect daily metrics after the app has inexplicably opted to switch back to weekly averages. So the experience of navigating data is very jumbled, with numbers bouncing all over the place, again even when limiting data elections exclusively to single, specific, daily measures. I'm also dissatisfied with the way that sleep tracking data set is presented. The level of detail and granularity is a downgrade from what was available on the previous Fitbit app. For instance, it used to be possible to see exactly how fractured sleep was broken down into periods of sleep and brief waking, but the new graphs make that impossible, only accounting for long periods of waking - periods of actual wakefulness are magically transformed into periods of sleep. At best, users of the new Google Health app will come away with only a vague sense of their sleep rather than the detailed analysis provided in the previous app. While I hope that this changes, I will immediately be looking for a new device from another company to take the place of my Fitbit because what Google provides now is not at all acceptable from a standpoint of accuracy and reliability.

text: I have used Google Health ever since I was forced to switch over to it on my Fitbit. I’ve been trying to get used to it, but it is very inaccurate in measuring my sleep, which is one of the primary reasons I use it. When I get up at night to go to the bathroom, it will often send me a message saying I had a poor night sleep even though I am far from getting up. This can be very distracting. Also, once you get a bad sleep score it often does not update the sleep score later, even if you go back to bed and sleep for hours. And it will often record a greater amount of sleep, and then in 15 or 20 seconds subtract out time you were awake during this time. Since I often use it to try to determine whether I have had enough sleep to get up, can be very distracting. Also, it will try to pick up activity during the day and identify what I I am doing, often recording that I am mountain biking when I am hiking up in the mountains. Or that I am hiking when I am actually road cycling ycling. This app needs a complete update, or needs to returned to the old Fitbit app. If they switch all of us to this, it needs to be an improvement. That is not the case.

title: The devs didn’t learn from their predecessors
text:
The app offers the basic features you’d expect from a health tracking app at a lower price point, with no subscription fees. That’s a solid selling point, but the execution needs work.

My biggest frustration is the lack of control over my own workout data. When the app overestimates my treadmill distance by a quarter mile, I should be able to correct it. Tracking errors happen. Preventing users from fixing them is a design choice—and a bad one. Guardrails are for rollercoasters, not my exercise log.

And why do I need Wi-Fi or cell service just to select a workout and start logging it? That’s basic functionality that should work offline, especially in an app people use while exercising.

For a Google app, this feels underwhelming. The price is appealing, but users need editable workout data, reliable offline functionality, and more control over their experience.

title: Not a fan
text:
First of all - the actual software engineers did an excellent job - from what I can tell so far.  My one star isn’t for them. My one star is for the very clear financial agenda of leadership who drove this update.

Before the update - if you wanted to dig deeper into a metric, you’d tap a visual. Now- when you tap almost any visual- you’re prompted to use their Google Health coach…even if you’ve already declined to use it.
They’ve also moved metrics so they aren’t at the forefront.  (Seriously?!? That’s the whole point of the app!!) Things like choosing one of their canned exercises and their commercial messages are now the center of attention. 
I’ve worked in software development for almost 20 years - and I can tell you with no uncertainty that forcing a complete overhaul of the user interface is HORRIBLE for end user satisfaction. Not to mention - taking the app update wasn’t even an option.  But this change wasn’t about the users… it was about their money and their data. 
Listen Google … not everyone wants AI integrated into every aspect of their lives. Not everyone is keen on giving up their data freely. And - some of us just want to view our data and make our own inferences.  
I’m ditching my premium subscription. I’m ditching my Fitbit.

title: Great hardware held hostage by a brainless app
text:
I bought the $99 Fitbit Air to escape the wrist-screen doom-scroll. The tracker itself is actually great, but because it doesn't have a screen, you are entirely chained to the new Google Health app—and this app feels like it’s actively trying to sabotage my gains.

First, the UI is a joke. You can't just drag and drop widgets on your home screen. If you get the order wrong, you have to delete every single one and start over from the top like it's 2010.

Then there’s the built-in AI "coach." It confidently hallucinates food macros, and its understanding of exercise is purely comedic. It completely locks you out of making quick manual adjustments mid-workout. Want to log a Farmer's Walk or hit the sauna post-workout? The AI refuses to use a simple timer and forces you to log it as "sets and reps." Yes, let's all go crush 3 sets of 10 "sitting and sweating."

As an iPhone user, the experience is basically hostile. Google completely ignored iOS lock screen widgets, Live Activities, and even basic notification badges. If you want to check your rest timer or current set, you can't just glance at your phone. You have to pick it up with chalky, sweaty hands, pray Face ID recognizes your grimacing face, and manually open the app. Every. Single. Time.

But the ultimate sin is the mid-workout crash. The app randomly closed during a heavy session yesterday. When I reopened it, the AI cheerfully acknowledged I was in the middle of a mapped workout, but completely forgot all the weights, extra sets, and micro-adjustments I had just logged. I was forced to recreate my entire session from memory while oxygen-deprived.

Two stars because the screenless hardware is comfortable, but this software is currently more frustrating than a bench press plateau. Give it a pass until the engineers actually try working out with it.

title: Don’t think, just download it!
text:
This app has been a lifesaver for my family. Yes most of the features are things that come standard on any smartphone, however the convenience of having (almost) everything in one place has helped this busy Dad and Mom get more organized.

We downloaded this initially for the Recipe Box and Meal Planner tools (premium features). Add your favorite recipes to your recipe box, plan your meals, and it automatically adds the ingredients to your list. The amount of time we save each week on meal planning and grocery lists has been well worth the monthly fee!

There are a few features that are lacking and some I’d love to see incorporated.

99% of the time I use the app on my phone and when adding a new task or item to your list, it doesn’t allow you to categorize it until after you have submitted it, sending that to the “uncategorized” section at the bottom of the list. Being able to categorize it when you initially enter the data would save some clicks/time.

Another feature that could use an upgrade is the calendar. It’s nice being able to import your calendar, but integrating it so that you can create an event in the app and have it show up in your default calendar app would be a welcomed update. 

Add some iOS widgets (calendar, notes, todo, shopping list, etc.) 

A wishlist item would be Life360 integration or replacement. The maps is very basic and unreliable. We have noticed inaccuracy in the locations, delayed or non-existent notifications when leaving/arriving at one of our set places. Life360 is an excellent tool for not only location services, but also crash detection, driving summary, and more.

That being said. Don’t think, just download it!

text: Overall this is a really cool app with so much potential to help my family be organized but the limited functionality of the task entry interface in lists prevents me from using this. If you edit a task the category to which it was assigned changes to uncategorized from whatever category you had originally tagged the task. It is a pain to recategorize because you have to click a separate button on the app or web interface to categorize a task. If the developer could make two changes this problem would be eliminated: (1) stop changing a task to “uncategorized” just because the name/title of the task is changed and (2) create a task entry interface that allows the user to (a) categorize the task at the same time that the task is created and (b) select the status of the task (undone, done, in progress, on hold) in the same interface with which the task is created (right now you have to create a task in a little field, then once the task is created you have to click another button to assign a category to the task, then click save, and click a third button to mark complete — all of this should be able to be in one interface, even if there remains a “quick add” field for adding uncategorized tasks). It takes so much more time than just being able to type in the time like any other calendar, and when you have so much to add with so much math to calculate, it just makes it so much more difficult to calculate and remember when you’re taking forever to scroll. 

Second thing: the “custom” repeat isn’t really custom. Being able to say, “this happens Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday,” like other apps would be so much easier than having to make an event on each of those days that repeats every week (and then having to edit individually when there is any change).

title: Fantastic sanity saving app with one issue..
text:
I’d like to start by saying how much my family loves and appreciates this app.  I have OCD, so organization and planning is a huge part of my life.  I use FamilyWall every day, and it is DEFINITELY worth the premium price.  I mainly use the calendar, meal planner, recipe box, and lists. 

The calendar is fantastic because you can change the colors to better organize each event.  You can do recurring events.  I also love the layout of events and the way it shows the colored dots on the days that have something on the calendar. 

I love the recipe box and meal planner SO MUCH.  You can write in your own recipe, or make it a million times easier by using a link from a recipe online and FamilyWall enters it in for you.  It’s so helpful to have a list already there of our favorites and even some recipes we haven’t tried yet. 

I love the lists function too because, well, OCD and lists.  Lol.  

I have recently started using the budget function, and honestly, I was shocked to be disappointed with it.  There is a glitch showing that I’m way over budget even though I have entered in my income.  The income doesn’t show up unless you switch to a different week, then back to the week you’re working on.  Even then, it sometimes doesn’t fix it.  

I also don’t like that you can’t have separate spending limits for bills vs other expenses.  I would do away with the spending limit that covers all of the categories, and just stick with the page after that that allows you to enter in spending limits individually for each category.  I’d like to have some categories that don’t have a spending limit, but it restricts that because you have to have a limit for each category or it shows over budget.  It’s kind of redundant to have to budget the bills on the budget then have to do it again on spending limits because you already know your overall limit based on your income.  For me personally, I’d rather be able to separate bills and other categories because I don’t really have a choice on how much my bills are, so there’s no point in having a “limit” for how much they’ll be. 

My last issue is that there isn’t an option for money left from the week before to carry over into the next week, so you have to enter it as “income” the next week.  This, along with the other issues, is pretty frustrating because I do love this app so much, but I think I may have to find a different app for budgeting which also means talking my family into downloading yet another app.

I will say that the budgeting function has huge potential to be great.  I love that you can choose how often it reoccurs, and you can customize the days rather than just generic options like “daily, weekly, monthly”, etc.  It’s helpful to have that function because a lot of subscriptions come out every thirty days rather than every month on the same date.  I love that it calculates how much you have left to spend.  It gives me so much peace of mind knowing how much I actually have left to spend compared to looking at my bank account which always takes days for the payments to actually show.  I know exactly how much I have left to spend with this app!

Overall, I’m extremely happy with FamilyWall.  My only complaint would be with the budgeting function, and I’m looking forward to seeing improvements to it and adding another star back to my review.  Thank you for taking the time to create an app like this!  You guys are the reason my home runs smoothly and that I’ve remained sane!

title: Excellent Organizer for Multi-Person Groups
text:
Instead of my family using this app, I use it with my home healthcare aides to create Task lists & grocery lists. I do use the Calendar for public appts only since I haven’t been able to figure out how to make certain appts only show up on my calendar /private from my aides. Thus, I’m still having to use two calendars. 

First, the good stuff:
1. Easy to use the calendar for joint events 
2. Easy to use the app to create joint (or private/individual) lists /tasks. 
3. Great way to create a grocery list where everyone can contribute 

I’m stumped on a few things that I haven’t figured out yet on the app:
1. Can I create appts on the calendar that are for just me to see? 

2. Is there a way to organize Tasks by priority, the ability to move them around since they put them in order of when they’re created. 
Note: You can filter by person it was assigned to. However, I’d like to prioritize their individual list, or be able to move things up/down within the master list. 

Overall, it offers a lot for joint use but could still use a few more options, especially being able to move items on the task list and having items marked completed automatically moved to another folder/area since they remain at the bottom of the list simply crossed off. I have to manually delete each one or they’ll always show up. 

Also, an option to print a list would be nice! Some kids don’t have phone access (my grandsons) & i know my son would love to easily create their list, print & hang up

title: Too Many Forced Distractions
text:
Thank you for fixing the lockup with the “walking“ feature, which trapped users in an inescapable software backwater. Much appreciated. I have one other request: Can you please give us a choice to opt out of the app’s many functions that we don’t want?

Case in point: Please make it possible to remove references to MyFitnessPal, software that I used long ago, but not anymore, because it has been surpassed by its far more sophisticated rival, Cronometer. 

It would also be helpful if we could opt out of your questionably useful “Today’s Missions”, which are poorly executed and profoundly outdated, often focusing on studies that have been paid for by companies that can benefit from them. 

Some people might like these extras, but I find them completely useless and distracting. I value ability to control the powerful features of your hardware, but not at the expense of having to be distracted and annoyed by unnecessary fluff. 

Simply let users choose whether we’d like to use these extras or not. This is especially relevant because now, unlike before, you are forcing us to wade through lots of distractions just so we can utilize the sophisticated features of your hardware, for which we already paid a premium price.

title: Great Hardware Ruined by a Greedy, Buggy App and Paywalled Basics
text:
I wish I could give zero stars. The physical scale/watch is fine, but the iOS app is an absolute disaster that makes the entire ecosystem worthless. Withings has completely lost touch with its user base, prioritizing subscription revenue over basic functionality.
 
The Paywall is Anti-Consumer: It is infuriating to spend hundreds on a device, only to have core health metrics locked behind the "Withings+" subscription. Users on the r/withings forum have repeatedly pointed out that features like Vascular Age and Electrodermal Activity (EDA) are suddenly restricted unless you pay up, even though these were previously accessible or promised as part of the hardware purchase . It feels like a bait-and-switch.‌￼
 
FDA Approval Means Nothing Here: You mentioned the FDA approval—it's a joke in this context. Even though Withings touts its FDA-cleared ECG, the app experience is so broken that the data is useless. Furthermore, users have discovered that even with FDA clearance, Withings still puts up arbitrary barriers (like requiring a "prescription" for ECG in the US) while simultaneously failing to deliver on basic data syncing . The hardware might be medically approved, but the software is not fit for purpose.‌￼‌￼
 
The App is Broken and Ignored: The recent updates (like 5.13 and the 2025 releases) have destroyed the user experience. The timeline is gone, it's cluttered with useless notifications, and data often fails to load . Worse, the sleep tracking and HRV scores have become wildly inaccurate and inconsistent since recent updates, with scores fluctuating overnight without any physical change . Customer service just ignores the flood of complaints .‌￼‌￼‌￼
 
Don't Buy It: Until Withings stops treating its paying customers as beta testers and stops holding basic health data hostage behind a subscription, do not buy their products. Avoid this app.

title: Worked for years, then Withings stopped supporting it
text:
My Withings Body scale worked well for years. Then one day, with no action on my part, it stopped recognizing users and stopped remembering prior weigh-ins. I reset it to fix that and it has not paired with my iPhone since. It gets stuck on the first setup step, every time. The cause is a known firmware incompatibility with current iPhones that Withings' own community forum has documented since October 2025 (search "Unable to pair and setup Body+ with iPhone 17 Pro"). The hardware is fine. Withings stopped keeping its firmware current, and the scale became a paperweight.

Customer support took almost two weeks of back and forth. Their first reply came in Catalan. They had me run troubleshooting steps I had already done, then concluded the scale needed replacing. Because it is outside the two-year warranty, the offer was 30% off a new scale, which now costs more than double what I paid. That is about $100 to replace a working product that Withings itself broke, with no reason to expect the next one would last any longer. Three rounds of asking for a supervisor or any better resolution got the same scripted answer.

A bathroom scale should not have an expiration date set by a phone update. If you want a scale that will still work in five years, buy one that doesn't depend on Withings keeping up.

title: Where is the data
text:
I just bought their latest scale model in body fit.


1 star — Plenty of distractions, no clear access to my data

I bought this Withings scale for the extensive body measurements advertised on the website. My main expectation was simple: step on the scale, open the app, and clearly see my measurements.

Instead, the app is cluttered with advertisements, unrelated content, and an intrusive AI assistant asking questions I have no interest in answering. Meanwhile, I cannot find a clear overview of the biomarkers that convinced me to buy the scale.

I can see some weight and body composition information, but even viewing basic measurements such as weight and body fat percentage feels unnecessarily difficult. If the other advertised measurements are available, I have not been able to find them.

The core problem is access to my own data. An expensive scale promising detailed measurements should make those measurements easy to view and track. In my experience, the app fails at that basic job.

title: They turned a bathroom scale into a subscription hostage situation
text:
Do NOT buy a Withings scale in 2026.

I bought Withings hardware to measure my weight, my body fat, my BMI and send it to Apple Health, where literally every other health device I own lives. That used to be the whole point of a smart scale.

As of October 13, 2026, Withings decided that basic feature is now a rent payment. Create a new Withings account today and you cannot export your own data to Apple Health or Health Connect unless you pay for Withings+ about $100/year. Not for coaching. Not for AI insights. Not for anything new. Just to move a number the scale you already paid for measured, from their app to Apple's app.

That's not a premium feature. That's a toll booth on your own data.

And don't let the "existing users are grandfathered" line fool you that's an admission, not a defense. They know current owners would revolt if they cut us off, so they're only screwing the next buyer who won't read the fine print until after setup, when they hit a paywall screen trying to turn on Apple Health sync. Your account gets deleted, you switch phones/emails, you set up a scale for your spouse/kid/parents? Welcome to the subscription.

This ruins the product. A smart scale that doesn't freely sync to Apple Health isn't smart, it's a walled garden with a glass platform. The hardware is now irrelevant I can't recommend a product whose business model is "buy the device, then pay us forever to actually use it in your health ecosystem."

Buy an InBody instead. The InBody Dial / H20N does proper 8-electrode body composition, syncs to the InBody app, and integrates with Apple Health, Google Fit, and Samsung Health with no subscription costs to access your body composition data. You buy it, you own it, it works. Revolutionary concept.

Withings used to be the easy recommendation. Now it's an easy warning: do not buy hardware from a company that will charge you rent to export your own weight.

title: Paywalling Apple Health sync
text: Withings now requires a paid subscription to sync any data to Apple Health (for now, it only affects accounts created after October 13th). This violates guideline 4.10 - “Monetizing Built-In Capabilities” - of the Apple App Review Guidelines (apps in the App Store are held to these guidelines), as HealthKit data writing is a native feature of Apple products that Withings is now paywalling. In addition, Withings advertising its products and apps as being Apple Health compatible, which violates Guideline 2.3 - “Accurate Metadata”. The new change means if you have a new account, your scale, for example, will no longer sync your weight and body composition data for free, which it used to be able to do. If you have an account created prior to October 13th, 2026, it’s only a matter of time before Withings paywalls the feature to the paid Withings+ subscription. Withings has already implemented scare tactics I have not appreciated: such as pushing sleep studies in a scary way: suggesting without adequate data that your sleep is concerning enough to warrant an at-home sleep study. The upsell appears as free but then it informs you that insurance will be used and it “may” be $0. This made me feel less happy with Withings already. Their support is abysmal and refuses to fix any feature that is broken. The app weight logs are often off by a month within the app, and in reporting this, it went nowhere. There’s a well-known bug when you click on your most recent exercise, it goes to a previous exercise day. The only positive is that Apple Health at least has been syncing the information accurately. text:
I bought a Withings Body Smart scale and BPM Connect blood pressure monitor. The hardware looks good and setup was easy. Then I discovered that Apple Health integration requires Withings+ for new accounts: $99.99/year or $9.99/month.

My measurements already sync to the Withings app on my phone. Charging a recurring fee to let that data reach Apple Health is ridiculous. I paid for the devices generating the measurements. Now I’m being asked to keep paying to use those measurements where I actually want them.

It feels like buying a luxury car and discovering the heated seats require a subscription. At least the car can blow my hair back and take me to dinner. This is a bathroom scale and a blood pressure cuff.

The app adds to the frustration by constantly pushing articles, guides, extra features, and subscription offers instead of simply putting my data front and center.

Support confirmed that my account falls under the new subscription requirement. This restriction should be impossible to miss before purchasing either device.

Apple Health integration was a major reason I bought these products. Finding it locked behind a subscription after buying and setting everything up was a punch in the gut. Had I known, I would have spent my money elsewhere.

This app lets me look at interactions and information about my medications if I want to.  I can change the time of a single or a group of meds just for one time or even skip one or all.  I can change the looks of the meds by shapes and colors so certain ones stand out.  I can delete meds and still keep the history of the med, or even just suspend the med.  This app really does it all.
I only have one complaint.  I wish more and different voices were periodically added.  I would pay a little extra for that because I have been listening to the same ones now for many years.  All-in-all, this is truly the best medication reminder app available (and I have tried them all!)

title: Not a trustworthy company
text:
I’ve been using this app for a long time, and now the developers have decided to introduce a subscription model. Some time ago, they already removed features that had always been available. While this is probably legal, it feels untrustworthy. Now they are removing almost everything unless you pay for a subscription.

Most apps don’t take away existing features; they usually add new options that users can choose to purchase.

I’ve been critical in the past and shared feedback—especially about how the app handles crossing time zones—but nothing meaningful ever changed. The developers clearly don’t understand how meditation should work when travelling across time zones, and the result is seriously flawed.

What surprises me most is that Apple offers the same features for free. Why would anyone choose this app if it doesn’t provide more value?

title: Such a bad user experience, it's potentially DANGEROUS.
text:
What an awful user experience. When setting up the meds, it turns out that 3x a day is NOT the same as "every 8 hours"—even though this is how hospitals do it. So it crams 3 doses into less time than intended, which is potentially dangerous. 

Next, the pill reminder is borderline unusable. There are 3 different views of your medications and schedule, and they each contain different information. The primary view doesn't even show my next dosing time. Why?

And if you take a dose late or early, it DOESN'T take that into account in your next dose (!!!!). So users, especially those who may have cognitive decline, can easily double up on dangerous meds like painkillers. 

This app is DANGEROUS, unusable, and embarrassingly bad. No clue how it has top ratings. Use Apple Health or write it down manually; don't risk your health.

title: Need an easy, quick way to track medicines. This app is neither quick nor easy.
text:
I need a simple, painfully basic app when I’m trying to just keep track of medications.

That’s why having to create an account or do anything involving my email, or seeing a clunky, overly complicated user interface will always result in a delete from me.

Like really…? This needs to be a service?

Dear developers everywhere: we don’t like creating accounts. We don’t like verifying emails. We don’t like using any Apps to help us do something that takes longer to do than the thing the App is supposed to help us do.

title: Use it every day. Wish it had a few additions/changes.
text:
I use this app every day to track my dogs' medications. I wish I could add an account for myself without having to pay for the pet account, but here we are. Despite that, I would love to see a small image – similar to the ones used to describe the pills or medications people take – for the medications my dogs are on. For example, my dog is currently taking two medications: one for breathing and one for his heart. It would be helpful to see a heart icon next to the time he is due for his heart medication, like "5:00 AM (heart)," and a lung icon next to the breathing medication, like "7:00 AM (lungs)." I know this might seem like a small detail, but it would help me keep everything organized at a glance.

Lastly, it would be incredibly useful to have an option for cut pills. My dog needs to take a quarter of a pill, but it's only listed as 0.25; I find "1/4" much easier to understand when it comes to his dosage.

title: Was nearly perfect until aggressive popup ads broke it
text: I’m a long time user of Medisafe, it has been an essential app for reliably tracking a lot of meds for chronic illness. A few days ago the app started an aggressive marketing campaign of full screen pop-ups that have broken the app. I can’t even mark a med as taken without the pop-up freezing in the middle of it. Because of this confusion and trying to get the app started again and again, then getting rid of the pop-up, we’ve actually missed marking some essential meds and not knowing if they were taken or not. I am happy to support and to purchase Medisafe, but this feels like maybe the company has been sold and we’re not dealing with the same people, feels sketchy and it might be time to look for an alternative. It’s a shame because this was really an excellent app. We fully rely on it being dependable as we juggle a heavy medicine routine and I haven’t found another app that worked as well.  I hope this isn’t the end of Medisafe.

text:
For two days, since the “Premium Access” update message box started popping up on my phone, my Medisafe app hasn’t run properly. When I decline the upgrade offer the upgrade box goes away, but then a little icon (I call a flower-clock) goes round and round, and I’m not able to access my medication.  If I close it out and reopen the app it starts over again with the “Premium upgrade” offer, then the rotating icon (flower).

Do not tell me to remove the app and re-download it, because if I have to reload all my meds again then I will download a different app altogether.  This issue has caused my opinion of the app to drop from a 5-star to a 1-star rating.

Major  suggestion besides fixing the above glitch…   provide an option to “permanently decline” account upgrade to “Premium.“ And then don’t allow  the upgrade option message pop-up box appear on that users account anymore.  Have the option for upgrade in their account management settings instead. Or create an upgrade option button icon at the bottom of the screen, below the meds list.

After the surgery there was a dosage error with one of the prescriptions which caused my heart rate to steadily drop into a very dangerous zone, and I slipped back into afib. If undetected, that could have also been dangerous.

Once again Kardia mobile detected it and I was able to send the graph to my electrophysiologist (who had done the surgery) who gave me instructions to quit the medication and come back for a cardioversion treatment immediately.

I am a huge fan and very thankful for it.

title: Buggy and dangerous
text:
I'd stopped using Garmin for cycling a few years ago because of all the bugs. But last year I crashed while alone in the woods and didn't have a computer with crash detection. So I decided to get a Garmin 1050 for the big screen and crash detection.  Fortunately I haven't needed it. But unfortunately it probably wouldn't have worked anyway. Twice now I've been going through the settings on my bike computer looking for something else and realized it said I didn't have an emergency contact so crash detection wouldn't work. It happened in March, and while I'm sure I had done it before, I redid my wife as emergency contact. And tested it to confirm the text message arrived. Just now I again found the computer said there wasn't an emergency contact and needed to set one up in the app. Checked and the app showed my wife with a verified phone number. I then verified her email and now the computer shows her verified and testing get assistance sends the phone text and email. And her phone shows the previous test from March. So I don't know when it broke, but at some point I lost that safety feature due to another Garmin bug. 

Feature bugs are one thing, but this is a safety bug. At least she would have my live track, which has never broken, but I hate that I bought a computer for a safety system that is too buggy to trust. (and I have no way of knowing whether the bug is the app or computer but the contact setup is in the app)

title: Could be so much better
text:
Garmin Connect provides excellent fitness data, advanced metrics, and workout functionality, but the music/download experience desperately needs improvement.

Managing downloaded playlists and music on a Forerunner 265 is unnecessarily difficult. There should be a simple option in Garmin Connect to view what music is currently downloaded to the watch, add or remove playlists, and force a music refresh directly from the phone. Instead, updating playlists requires navigating through the watch itself and relying on a separate Wi-Fi sync process.

For a smartwatch with otherwise excellent training functionality, this feels outdated and unintuitive. Please make music management part of Garmin Connect and allow users to manage and refresh watch downloads directly from the app.

title: Superior Data
text: After having 4 Apple Watches I grew tired of the hamster wheel approach to activity tracking and goals. I was also tired of switching between watches because none of them could last a full day and night for sleep tracking. I purchased an entry level Forerunner and was blown away with how superior both the data and battery were. Intelligent data that was actually useful and only needing a charge once a week? What a dream. The user interface on the app isn’t quite as polished as Apple and has a bit of a learning curve but it’s not that bad; I picked it up quick. There is a lot you can do with building workouts, setting goals, tracking gear and the like. I feel like I use a lot of it but at the same time know I haven’t even scratched the surface really. I thought I would miss smart notifications and some functions more than I do, but I’ve actually enjoyed having a watch that is more watch than a very small not as useful phone on your wrist. Two years in now, absolutely no regrets I’d rebuy this Forerunner 100x over another Apple Watch. I still get nearly 7 days of battery and it works just as good as the first day I wore it. I’ll upgrade eventually but I can tell it won’t be caused by need like all my Apple Watches…it will be my choice. And I’m planning to get a higher end Forerunner that will give me even more useful data — worth every penny!

The Garmin Connect app and my new Instinct watch are both very awkward to navigate: 
-Too many menus and submenus
-Initial view/home pages are nearly useless for everyday use: you have to go hunt through menus
-Data is presented in Garmin-ese tech metrics: sleep score, VO2X(?) title: I can’t take it anymore. Unfortunately I must give a bad review.
text: I am at my wit’s end with this app. I have been using it for years and years and years. It used to mostly work right. The buggiest thing I experienced is having to force quit it and re-open in order to get it connect to my watch. That used to always solve the problem of lack of connection. But a few months ago, maybe even a year, something changed and now it’s extremely common (normal) that when I open the app, not only is it not showing a connection to my watch, but force quitting no longer solves the problem. I now have to go into Settings, turn off Bluetooth, I wait 10 seconds, turn Bluetooth back on, then go back to Garmin Connect and at that point, finally, it has usually established a connection with my watch (but not every time!). WHY DO I HAVE TO DO THIS!? WHY HAS THIS BEEN GOING ON FOR MONTHS AND MONTHS AND MONTHS AND GARMIN HASN’T FIXED IT YET!? I feel like it’s driving me slowly insane and now tonight what really pushed me over the edge to write this review is that I had to go through this rigamarole TWICE maybe about an hour apart (an hour which included my run, and the app failed to announce my splits as it’s supposed to, probably because it had lost the connection). PLEASE FIX THIS STUPID FREAKING, OBNOXIOUS, TIME-WASTING PROBLEM, GARMIN! I BEG OF YOU!!!!!

title: Doesn’t work well with iOS!!
text:
I live several states away from my mother so I was relieved to hear that I could locate her in an emergency. Except the GPS is lousy. It seems to reliably report if she’s home or “out and about” but it almost never tells me where she is exactly. Even when she’s home—and they have her address on her record—it puts her up to a couple miles away. Sometimes it says she’s in another city. A few times she’s been in the middle of a river! (And she doesn’t know how to swim.) 

After some searching I’ve learned that this has been a common glitch with iOS. You’d think this would be important enough to fix but apparently not. Luckily she’s not one to wander off (yet?) but if she ever were to do so this app would be useless.

title: “Lively Mobile +” with Fall Detection ✅
text:
Only three days after receiving my “Lively Mobile+” medical alert device, I bent over to pick up something small I had stepped on in my bare feet. 
The next thing I knew, I had crumpled and was sitting upright, on the floor, blankly looking around. (I’ve had a degenerative muscle condition for 30 years). 
I had began thinking “Well, That was unexpected!”
Then I heard a pleasant, confident voice greeting me by name… from my device:
“Mrs. Pearson your device indicates you had a fall. Are you alright?” Or something similar to that. She also asked several questions checking in my condition. Did I hit my head?, was I injured? etc. Which were all great because a hard fall can leave me befuddled a bit at first. 
Next she asked permission to put me on hold while she called Emergency Services and for me to please stay on the line. 
She was soon back to me and waited with me until Emergency Services showed up. The the call was pleasantly ended. 
Sign me: A Happy, Protected Customer
————
Note - the device runs on a full charge for approximately 80 hours. 
If it runs low, an unusual beep sounds … Even at 2:30 in the morning. 
I have decided mark Charging Days on my calendar until it is a habit. 
————
Special Note - I expected the device to be annoying to wear. I think I even wanted to hate it because it represented another stage of becoming more disabled. 
I was 100% wrong. 
Instead of being annoying, it is comfortable and I was surprised with how quickly I became adjusted to wearing it all the time. 
Favorite Detail about the “Lively Mobile+” model - My particular medical insurance paid for the device and all the monthly fees. 
If you’re considering this device, at least give your insurance company a call and see if it is covered or helpful on the costs. 
Since I live alone, my family and other loved ones are glad I took this step forward towards safety. They also like the free “Lively Link” app (shows clasped hands on the icon) where they can find out if I’ve had falls or been out and about. The GPS feature helps with that.

2)  RESPONSE IS HORRIBLE!!!  Last week my mother had an episode and hit the button on her pendant. Due to the fact she passed out, she was unable to answer any questions from the dispatcher.  Emergency services were never called and occasionally the company would call her home phone to see if she picked up. Finally, after 40 MINUTES I receive a call from GreatCall stating they are unable to get into contact with my mother and request I check to ensure her safety and call them back.  REALLY??  40 MINUTES BEFORE THE FIRST CALL IS PLACED TO A POINT OF CONTACT??

3) APP IS TERRIBLE!!!  I already mentioned the GPS flaws, the response to emergencies not being even par, but finally the clunky app.  The app keeps a log of every time the button is pressed, which is great!!!  Too bad it doesn’t update until the next day!!!  The quickest I’ve ever received an app notification was 5 HOURS LATER!!!  

The sad thing is I pay extra for all these features, I think like $38/month for the highest package.  I’m not sure what else exists on the market but a tin can telephone for communication coupled with a jingle bell collar is quite comparable.

title: Works well enough.
text: I used this app for a few weeks and I'm finding ways to get what I need from it. From the reviews, I'd say expectations are a little high. I get reasonable results by closing the app between uses. I don't logout, I just bring up my list of loaded apps and "X" this one so that it opens fresh each time. To get a current location update, I open the app and click the refresh button. After it starts showing dots across the screen, I close the app ("X" out from the list of loaded apps). When I reload the app 5 minutes later, the updated location is available. I don't know why it takes time. Maybe it's a batch operation running on a mainframe computer. We get piece of mind from this app, in spite of the fact that results aren't instantly available. The service that answers calls seems terrific. We are very satisfied. If you seek software perfection, you may need to keep looking. This isn't self-contained technology like some game on your phone. You're trying to track down an inexpensive cellular device that may be roaming between cell towers. This one isn't perfect but it does the job and the app costs nothing.

I was very upset my 92 year old mom was left without a lanyard and they are expecting IRMA a cat. 5 hurricane to hit Florida this week. I would not recommend this alert system unless they fix the LANYARD issue.

title: Inconsistent coverage
text:
I am linked to this app to keep me in touch with an elderly friend I assist. Frequently the app will say that the device is off or not in service.  When I contact my friend, his device is working but I don't have access because my link is not working. I spoke with technical support who told me to logout, turn off my mobile phone and wait a few minutes and then turn the phone back on and log in. It fixed the problem when I was talking with tech support.  However, today I had the same problem.  I tried logging out, turning off my phone about 3 different

 times. Continued to state the device was either turned off or out of service.  I deleted the app and downloaded the app again. When I logged in I got the same message. Again I logged out n then turned off my phone for a few minutes and then went through the process of turning my phone back on and logging in again.  It now shows that the device is on and the battery is charging. My friend is diligent about wearing the device and charging it nightly.  If I can not get consistent and accurate information from my link that is a problem.  Also, it is concerning that technical support is not available 24/7. If this device is meant to aid the elderly or persons with medical issues technical support should be available or at least have a tech person on call that can handle any incoming request for assistance.  This is my 1st experience with Great Call and it's device.  At this time I am frustrated with the inconsistency and the lack of tech staff to assist outside of regular  customer service hours.  I hope improvements will be made.

Frustrated caregiver

title: Great Call to Unreliable Call
text: Has gone from excellent to TRASH. Have been a very happy user for FOUR YEARS until lately. Am still researching, talking with tech support, and am actually riding around to field test problems. We used to get 95%+ success in locating wearer. Now we get maybe 10% success. Same house. Same car. Same town. Same frequent destinations. Small town. No new developments. There is a Verizon tower about 2 and 1/2 miles from house. It appears the issue is that the Lively Mobile device is 3G technology and what Verizon tells me is it gets lowest priority on 4G towers so it will be slower and slower to update and may get shut out entirely during more busy times. That explains why sometimes ( rarely now) it succeeds in seconds and other times ( more frequently) it tries forever and still fails. As more towers convert to 4G these other reviewers that are singing it's praises as I once did will be left behind as well.  As per just the app, it too is flawed. The info it gives you does NOT really mean what it says. It could be HOURS old yet it tells you wearer was at a location, say, 10 minutes ago. It simply IGNORES all the failed attempts. There is more; that's just one example. I may update after field test. System is failing. App doesn't account for failure thus making it inaccurate.

title: Not good from my perspective

I thought she was having a problem and frightened her with a call at that time of night.  It often shows her out when she's home during the day. What good is that? I'm a firefighter and I respond to people who use these types of services and the locations are accurate and I recommend them. I don't trust this system, and will look into something else.

title: Phone is great, but..........
text:
